Prima SI p.211 says the creeper 'immediately leaves its brood the moment it spawns'. In our world the brood is the ixthiar nest: Ixthiar Broodmother at local (22268,18223), plus the dense nest of 12 faction-87 ixthiar decimaters at local X 17-21k, Y 17.5-22k, ringed by reapers and doomcallers. That matches the Warcry Fylara's Armor spoiler, whose nest is 'across the wooden bridge and to the northwest' on the road SW from Aalid Feie; Fylara is at local (48258,21954). Home spawn is on the east side of that nest, between the decimaters and the Broodmother: local (21000,19000) = world (283144,346680). Z: K.ground/groundz165 gives no floor anywhere in zone 183 (it even fails at existing mob spots), so Z 3725 is the mean of the 4 nearest live rows (3710, 3712, 3727, 3760; all within 64). A post-period Allakhazam comment (2007-03-02) puts a creeper at loc 23639,11908, about 7k north of the brood inside the reaper/doomcaller field. That backs up 'wanders out into the vale' but was not used as the spawn point.
monsters.script:
PERIOD EVIDENCE
(1) Prima Shrouded Isles (2002), Vale of Balor, 'Enhanced Monster AI' box (txt line 29691; layout line 9414): 'A creeper immediately leaves its brood the moment it spawns. It then ventures out into the vale and starts spawning more ixthiar. If there are no players to control the ixthiar, they will spread over 1/3 of the entire area.' SI Prima monster table: level 45 (the layout text's '42-45' is a two-row column shift; si_tables.json and Allakhazam both give 45).
(2) Allakhazam/Illia bestiary cmob=5511, Wayback capture 2003-09-19 (entry last updated 2003-01-08): Insect, 'Creepers are known to leave it's brood and wander out into the open and spawn babies, and can possilby cover 1/3 the area', min/max level 45, Vale of Balor, lowers Ixthiar Swarm. No loot, no comments in period.
(3) Post-period only, corroboration not authority: the live ZAM page (updated 2007) adds 'when pulling one also brings a Ixthiar Decimater', a 2007-03-02 comment gives loc 23639,11908 'in the Ixthiar Woods', and it lists the loot.
(4) Prima SI zone text (p.208): ixthiar are 'social pack MOBs and have the ability to call for help when outnumbered'; bring crush weapons.
No period source gives a respawn timer, a spawn interval, an add count or the add type beyond 'more ixthiar'/'babies'. Those values below are marked CHOICE.

WHAT EXISTS IN THE SERVER: nothing for this encounter. No class or brain mentions ixthiar or creeper (I grepped GameServer scripts, namedmobs, ai/brain, quests and mode165). Patterns to reuse:
- scripts/mobs/Strangler.cs and BotonidSeedling.cs: a GameNPC subclass that calls SetOwnBrain(new XBrain()) in AddToWorld. The Mob row then carries ClassType 'DOL.GS.Scripts.<Class>' with Brain '' or 'DOL.AI.Brain.<Brain>'; the DB already does this for DOL.GS.Scripts.Strangler / DOL.AI.Brain.StranglerBrain.
- scripts/namedmobs/Galladoria/SpindlerBroodmother.cs SpawnSplinder() + class SBAdds: timer-spawned adds with RespawnInterval = -1, LoadedFromScript = true and their own faction, never saved to the DB.
- scripts/mobs/AlbionMobs/Eques.cs: Body.WalkTo(point, speed) for walking legs.
- ai/brain/StandardMob/BafFriends.cs: the existing faction 'call for help' covers Prima's social-pack note through faction 87. No new code is needed for that.
NEW CODE NEEDED: class DOL.GS.Scripts.IxthiarCreeper : GameNPC and brain DOL.AI.Brain.IxthiarCreeperBrain : StandardMobBrain. The spawn row uses ClassType 'DOL.GS.Scripts.IxthiarCreeper', Brain 'DOL.AI.Brain.IxthiarCreeperBrain' (or '' if the class sets its own brain), NPCTemplateID 60162558, FactionID 87, Level 45, RoamingRange 0 (the brain does the walking).

BEHAVIOUR SPEC
A. Spawn and respawn (period: Prima 2002 and Allakhazam 2003): the creeper appears at the home spot (the brood). On AddToWorld, without waiting for an idle tick, it picks a first destination 1500-3000 units from home, pointing away from the nest centre (local 19500,19700), and walks there at speed 191 (template MaxSpeed). This is 'immediately leaves its brood'.
B. Wandering (period: 'ventures out into the vale'/'wander out into the open'): while it has no aggro, each time it arrives (or every 20-40 s if stuck) it picks a new leg 1000-2500 units long, biased outward until it reaches the leash edge, then random. CHOICE, clamped to the SPREAD AREA: zone-183 local X 8,000-45,000, Y 5,000-37,000. That is the bounding box of all live ixthiar in the vale (X 10.4k-47.1k, Y 7.0k-35.1k) plus a margin, about 1.18e9 units², roughly 28% of the 65536² zone ≈ Prima's '1/3 of the entire area'. Exclude a 4000-unit radius around the Grove of Aalid Feie (local ~49600,25000) and do not path into the Fomorian town to the south (local Y > 37k). Region 181 has no usable navmesh in the helper, so use straight WalkTo legs and keep Z by the server's normal ground follow.
C. Seeding more ixthiar (period: 'starts spawning more ixthiar'/'spawn babies'). Every 90-180 s (CHOICE, random each time), while the creeper is alive, out of combat and inside the spread area, it places ONE offspring at its current position (±100 units).
  - Offspring type, CHOICE: 'ixthiar decimater' from NpcTemplate 60162559, level 39-41 (Prima SI decimater levels), model 686, faction 87, RoamingRange 200 like the family rows, RespawnInterval -1, LoadedFromScript = true, CanDropLoot as normal decimater loot (the existing 'ixthiar decimater' MobXLootTemplate). Why decimater: it is the lowest-level ixthiar in the core wood, it makes up the brood cluster the creeper spawns from, and the post-period ZAM note says a creeper pull 'also brings a decimater'. Option: a weighted pick from decimater/reaper/doomcaller templates 60162559/60162562/60162560.
  - Population cap, CHOICE for the bot-scale rule: at most 24 live offspring per creeper. At the cap it keeps wandering but stops seeding until offspring are killed. This is how players 'control the ixthiar'.
  - Offspring persist after the creeper dies; they are not saved, so a server restart clears them. Never spawn an offspring within 1500 of a player-realm guard or town NPC.
D. Combat: an ordinary level-45 insect with no special attacks or abilities in any period source. Faction-87 social assist comes from the existing BafFriends. No adds at a health threshold (none recorded in period). It stops seeding and wandering while it has aggro. After combat it does NOT return to the brood: it resumes wandering from where it is (that is how it spreads). The template's TetherRange 4500 should be ignored or kept relative to the current position; otherwise it would yank the creeper back to the nest.
E. Death and respawn: the creeper respawns at the home spot after RespawnInterval and repeats A-C. 900 s is a CHOICE; there is no period figure (the family rows use 80-300 s, which would flood the vale). Keep exactly ONE creeper row; Prima describes 'a creeper' leaving 'its brood'.
F. Performance (bot scale 1-2k bots per realm): ThinkInterval of at least 1500 ms. Track offspring in a List on the creeper, not with region scans. Run the seeding timer as an ECSGameTimer only while alive.
G. Loot: no period drop is tied to the creeper. The existing MobXLootTemplate 'Ixthiar Creeper' (id 5511) points to an empty LootTemplate; leave it empty. Ixthiar Healing / Nature's Aid / Rejuvenating Stone existed in period (Freddyshouse sale posts 2003-09-21 and 2003-11-19; ItemTemplate rows Ixthiar_*_Stone exist, dropped by nothing in our DB). The only creeper link is the post-period ZAM loot list (page updated 2007), so adding them is an owner decision, not a period fact. Coin: Coin165 Insect body default.
RELATED, out of scope: our Ixthiar Broodmother is a fixed 300 s spawn. Period/early-2004 sources (Warcry Fylara's Armor spoiler, CSR reply 2004-04-11) say she pops in one of SIX large stumps once the reapers and doomcallers around the nest are cleared. That is a separate encounter.

monsters.script:
Parent encounter: CUINN (Mob_ID 100027804, Cothrom Gorge, Outlander Town). The seedlings exist only as Cuinn's adds.

PERIOD EVIDENCE
(a) Freddyshouse, old.Xanthian, 2003-03-13 18:33 UTC ('help with sc template') and 2003-03-17 ('They Mysterys of HyBrasil'). Cuinn is about level 65-70 and takes a beating. At 10% health he calls for help, and the whole town comes along with 6 treant seedlings that con red to a level 50. The seedlings drop the jewels, about 4-5 jewels per pull. Groups pulled Cuinn to the crossroads far from town so they could finish him before the adds arrived. Clearing the town before the pull means fewer adds.
(b) Patch 1.61 notes, quoted on Freddyshouse 2003-04-02: the drop rate for the garran treant seedlings that are part of the Cuinn encounter in Hibernia was adjusted to the appropriate level. The pre-1.61 rate was a bug (a player said he made about 30 plat from it).
(c) Prima SI, Cothrom Gorge monster table: garran treant seedling 60. Allakhazam cmob=5898 (captures 2003-04-19, last updated 2003-01-08): Plant, level 60-60, Cothrom Gorge. Killing it lowers faction with Z'zozicck Zhxizzckrrk, The Watcher, Tree of Ages and Outland Residents.
(d) Allakhazam items 8782, 8783 and 8784 (captured 2003-08/09) say each is dropped by the Garran Treant Seedling in Cothrom Gorge.
(e) Players could not find a seedling in the world (zam comments 2003-06-13 and 2003-06-28). This shows the seedlings are not static spawns.

TRIGGER
Cuinn is in combat and his HealthPercent drops to 10 or below. This fires once per spawn or reset cycle. The period wording of the shout is not recorded. Use a neutral broadcast such as 'Cuinn calls for help!', the same style as VagdushBrain.

SEQUENCE ON TRIGGER
1. Town call-for-help (period: 'the whole town comes along'). Take every living NPC of faction 98 (Outland Residents) within about 4500 units of Cuinn's SpawnPoint, not his current position. He may have been pulled to the crossroads, and period groups relied on the town having to travel to them. Copy Cuinn's aggro list to each of them (AddAggroListTo, as in VagdushBrain and AnurigundaBrain). Townsfolk who are already dead do not come, which matches 'clear the town first'. My suggestion, not period data: leave out service NPCs (Guild set: merchants, healer, smith, enchanter).
2. Spawn exactly 6 garran treant seedlings at Cuinn's SpawnPoint plus the offsets above, which is the town, not Cuinn's current spot. Each seedling gets RespawnInterval -1 and is put into combat against Cuinn's aggro list, starting with his current target. The seedlings then walk or run from town to the fight.

ADDS
6 x 'garran treant seedling': level 60, body Plant (10), model 946, size 50, FactionID 98, speed 191. Melee stats come from the garran treant template 60161210 with Level forced to 60. No NpcTemplate 'garran treant seedling' exists yet, so add one (based on 60161210, Level 60, Size 50) or set the values in code. The seedlings keep fighting after Cuinn dies, because the period groups killed Cuinn first and then the seedlings for the jewels. Do NOT kill them on Cuinn's death. This differs from ElroTheAncient.Die, which kills its adds.

RESET / DESPAWN
When Cuinn leaves combat (no aggro or wiped, CheckProximityAggro false), remove the seedlings that are still alive and clear the trigger flag. This is the AnurigundaBrain RemoveAdds pattern. Seedlings that outlive Cuinn and have no targets should go back to their spawn spot and be removed. A 60-second idle timer is an implementation choice, not period data. They never respawn on their own. The next set comes with Cuinn's next spawn. Cuinn's live RespawnInterval is 80 (seconds, multiplied by 1000 in GameNPC.LoadFromDatabase), which is very short for a named target. Period players farmed him repeatedly, but no period respawn time was found. Owner's call.

LOOT
MobXLootTemplate row 'garran treant seedling' -> LootTemplate 'garran treant seedling' already exists with DropCount 2. The LootTemplate has NO rows, so nothing drops today. Add Petrified_Treant_Seed, Crystalized_Treant_Seed and Frozen_Treant_Seed (all three ItemTemplates exist). Period rate: before the fix, about 4-5 jewels from the 6 seedlings of one pull. After the 2003-04-02 fix the rate was lowered to an unstated 'appropriate level', and the seeds were still farmed and sold in numbers in Sept 2003 (Freddyshouse WTS 2003-09-15, 'several of each'). No exact post-fix percentage exists. Pick a modest per-seedling chance and lower DropCount to 1. That is an owner/loot decision. Item data mismatches against period Allakhazam pages: Crystalized period is ML50, level to attain 49, but the DB says 47. Petrified (8782) period: 5 charges of a 95 cold DD. Frozen (8784) period: 5 charges of a 95 cold DD, 2.6 s cast. All three DB rows have SpellID 0 and Charges 0.

ALREADY IN THE SERVER
There is no Cuinn script, brain or seedling code anywhere in GameServer: grep for cuinn/seedling/treant finds only ElroTheAncient, Hurionthex, TheLostSeed quest, BotonidSeedling and a bot bench. The live Cuinn is a plain DOL.GS.GameNPC with Brain '' and FactionID 0, although his NpcTemplate 60159526 has FactionID 98. Patterns to reuse:
- scripts/namedmobs/Fomor/Anurigunda.cs: AnurigundaBrain spawns waves of adds once at 40% and 20% HP (RespawnInterval -1), removes them on reset, and BAFs PackageID-tagged NPCs. Its AnurigundaAdds class and AnurigundaAddsBrain show how an add class is built.
- scripts/mobs/AlbionMobs/Vagdush.cs: VagdushBrain calls for help once at 10% or below and copies its aggro list to nearby NPCs.

NEW CODE NEEDED
1. DOL.AI.Brain.CuinnBrain : StandardMobBrain, implementing the trigger, steps 1-2 and the reset above.
2. Optionally a DOL.GS.GarranTreantSeedling : GameNPC add class with its own brain, or plain GameNPCs built from the new NpcTemplate.

HOW THE SPAWN ROW REFERENCES IT
GameNPC.LoadFromDatabase builds the brain from Mob.Brain with ScriptMgr.GameServerScripts. On Mob 100027804, set Brain = 'DOL.AI.Brain.CuinnBrain' and ClassType stays DOL.GS.GameNPC; a DOL.GS.Cuinn class is an alternative. Also set FactionID = 98 so the Outland faction link works. The seedlings themselves get NO Mob rows.

(1) Allakhazam Skona Ravine zone page (cmzone=33), comment dated Jan 25 2002, which is before the cutoff: a party of level 36s was hunting 'in the deep ravine, were Wolverines are found ... right near the western end' when 'a Yecats came up and dropped us all'. Our navmesh shows a deep ravine floor at Z about 1450-2500, compared with about 5000 on the plateau. It runs from zone-local (14000,18000) through (22000,13500) to (30000,9400). The L39-40 'wolverine' rows (DB 13632,18023 / 14594,18062 / 25855,11862 / 30000,9400) and the radar wolverine clusters sit on that floor, so the western end is about x 14000-16000, y 14000-18000. (2) Prima Atlas Skona map label '^ECATS' (Atlas txt L29960; layout.txt line 10025, cols ~60-105). It is overprinted with ARACHITE PRIEST / ODIN'S SERVANT / YVER / YVER, just under GUNNOLFR and next to TIU EVIL / WEREWOLF CHAMPION. A least-squares fit of 19 named-mob labels against their DB positions (residual about 3-6k) puts it at about (20000-31000, 13000-18000) zone-local. That is the western/middle part of the same ravine, and the paired WEREWOLF CHAMPION label matches the DB champion at (22500,17163). (3) Kirstena 2002 map: no label for it. Chosen spawn: zone-local (18000,15500) = world (706128,916620), on the ravine floor between the Allakhazam 'western end' and the Prima label. Z = K.ground 1890, exact navmesh floor. RoamingRange 4000 covers both, and fits 'came up'. For reference only, not used: gorff's 2004 freddyshouse sighting is after the cutoff and on the plateau 'between the rope bridge ... and the guard tower', around Kirstena bridge (35-36k, 29-32k) and werewolf towers (39-42k, 26-31k).
monsters.script: NO SPECIAL ENCOUNTER: no period source describes adds, phases, timers or a trigger. Spec: one named L50 wyvern, aggressive, wandering the deep Skona ravine floor. TRIGGER: none, always up after respawn. BEHAVIOUR: (a) Standard melee aggro. Both period reports have it attacking without being pulled: Allakhazam Jan 25 2002 'came up and dropped us all' (a group of L36s); freddyshouse 2004-01-20 'popped right on top of me and killed me in about 3 hits ... about 159 dmg each hit'. (b) Roams: RoamingRange 4000 on the ravine floor. No PathID: there is no period patrol path. ADDS: none. DESPAWN: none. LOOT: none. Prima Atlas creature list L30764 'Yecats [50] (no loot)', so no ItemsListTemplate or LootTemplate rows; leave coin to the server's normal named-NPC rule, or set it to 0 to match 'no loot' strictly (owner's call). RARITY: players called it almost never seen: a 2-year player on freddyshouse 2004 had never seen it, it is in no Allakhazam bestiary entry, the CapnBry radar never logged it, and it is not on Uthgard. A long respawn (1800 s is my suggestion; no period timer exists) approximates that with no new code. A true chance-pop (e.g. a placeholder spawn with an X% chance to become Yecats) would need new code. Nothing in GameServer implements one: grep found no Rare/Placeholder/ChanceSpawn class. Do not build it unless the owner asks. ALREADY IMPLEMENTED: plain DOL.GS.GameNPC with the default StandardMobBrain (ClassType 'DOL.GS.GameNPC', Brain empty/NULL) covers aggro and roaming through the RoamingRange column. The spawn row should copy the savage wyvern base row (Mob_ID c55c6e81-…, NPCTemplateID 60165624: Race 2002, BodyType 3, FactionID 0, MeleeDamageType 3, Dex 96, Pie/Emp/Cha 30) and override Name 'Yecats', Level 50, Size 110, AggroLevel 100, AggroRange 500, RoamingRange 4000, RespawnInterval 1800, plus the X/Y/Z/Heading above. No class or brain exists for Yecats in scripts\namedmobs, ai\brain, quests or mode165: grep for 'yecats' over development-source\server finds nothing. PERIOD CONTEXT: the name is 'Stacey' reversed. Prima printed it in a pile of quest-encounter labels (Odin's Servant, Yver Tiu x2, Tiu Evil, arachite priest, Gunnolfr), which suggests a rare or Mythic-internal spawn, but two independent player sightings, in Jan 2002 and Jan 2004, show it really appeared in game.

monsters.script:
PARENT ENCOUNTER: the Unseelie Envoy convoy (Lough Gur / Bog of Cullen, region 200). The convoy is the envoy, 2 siabra escorts and 2 supernatural stallions walking a long route as one group. It is not a boss with adds called at % health. No period source mentions health-% adds, special attacks or despawns.

MEMBERS: 1 'unseelie envoy' (live row 96a684aa-74ce-44d7-9f7c-188451ca22e3, template 60167452, model 334 Elf Male 1; Prima lv55). 2 'supernatural stallion' (live rows d91bd52f-4837-4ae1-b1d4-17ed24eee52a and 470ade65-3d8c-4266-bd71-07e7d58623d6, template 60166634; Prima lv48; change model 2132 to 414 'Nightmare', the pooka look, because 2132 is not in the 1.64 client). 2 'siabra escort' (new, template 60165982). Today all of them are static DOL.GS.GameNPC rows with RoamingRange 200, and stallion 470ade65 stands 8k east of the others.

ROUTE (world coords, region 200):
(A) Home: the base of the Siabra Queen's tower in the Siabra city, Bog of Cullen. Queen Cliodna stands on the upper floor at 388237,752506,5722; the ground at the base is about 388637,752506,5040. Source: Verena, Freddyshouse, 2002-05-05: the group stands at the base of the Siabra queen tower.
(B) The land bridge near Siopa: 361569,745050 (ground 4959). Sources: the Zam bestiary loc '9313, 32346 Bog of Cullen' on all three mob pages (page updated 2008, loc not dated); boni_ofdavoid, Freddyshouse, 2003-02-04: they 'headed off to siabra city via the land bridge near Siopia'. The Siopa merchants are at about 361.3k,750.3k.
(C) Lough Gur, south-east, where the live envoy and stallions stand now: 334799,742184,6857 and 342198,742938,7255.
(D) The Lough Gur turnaround, near the pooka spawn west of Innis Carthaig: the Prima Atlas map label cluster at about 312400-315100, 702900-705600 (ground 4219-4624). Supporting posts: josua, 2002-10-09 ('Pookahs West of innis ... we have seen a convoy'); boni, 2003-02-04 ('from near the pook spawn at innis towards the bog').
HARD RULE: the route must NOT pass through Innis Carthaig (merchants and guards at 333.8-335.6k, 718.9-721.1k). Source: the 1.42 release notes (Warcry patchs/020115, about Jan 2002): 'A bug was found with the path of the Unseelie Envoy and his escort. His escorts and stallions should no longer ... cross through Innis to return home.' The straight line from D to B runs right through Innis, so the path must go D -> south around Innis (through C) -> B -> A. Build the in-between waypoints on the navmesh (K.ground); no period waypoints exist beyond A-D.

TIMING: one out-and-back trip: A -> B -> C -> D, short stop, D -> C -> B -> A, then rest at A. Source: Verena, 2002-05-05: 'Every morning they go out on a patrol all the way into Lough Gur and head back to the Siab town in the afternoon.' Patch 1.42 (before 1.64, so it applies) says 'This group may now also show up during the day or night (previously, he only came out in the day).' So do NOT time-gate the trip. Do NOT use DOL.GS.DaySpawn / NightSpawn. josua saw the convoy at night in 2002-10. Rest and stop lengths are not documented. Suggest about one trip per game day, starting at a random time.

COMBAT: (1) The whole convoy fights together: if any member is attacked or aggroes, all members join (escort social type 'Call' per Zam; Revised siabra 'Call'). (2) The stallions aggro even on high-level players. Source: old.Charonel, 2002-05-05: 'those horses had to be aggro ... the only things in the whole city that are aggro to me.' (3) Long chase leash: the convoy followed a fleeing player into Innis and fought the town guards until killed. Source: Alia_CBH, 2002-05-06: 'followed me to Innis and went on rampage in Innis ... 1 dead stallion and 1 dead guardian before the convoy was killed.' Our Innis already has the extra Sentinel Champions, Noble Steeds and Guardians. Verena says those were added because of this convoy. Those guards must be hostile to the convoy and fight it. (4) After combat, survivors regroup on the leader and the trip resumes from the nearest waypoint.

RESPAWN: no period data. Suggested: when every member is dead, the convoy respawns as one unit at A on the envoy's respawn timer, and the escort and stallion rows do not respawn on their own. Today they would respawn individually every 80s.

LOOT: envoy and stallions have none (Prima Atlas). Escort loot is listed in notes.

ALREADY IN THE SERVER:
- DB paths: tables Path (PathID, PathType, RegionID) and PathPoints (Step, X, Y, Z, MaxSpeed, WaitTime). EPathType: Once=1, Path_Reverse=2, Loop=3.
- A mob with Mob.PathID set walks the path by itself. StandardMobState_IDLE switches to PATROLLING when Body.CanMoveOnPath. StandardMobState_PATROLLING calls Body.MoveOnPath(MaxSpeed) and drops into AGGRO on proximity aggro (ai/brain/StandardMob/StandardMobState.cs). Path_Reverse (2), with WaitTime on the end points A and D, gives the out-and-back trip with rests.
- GameNPC.Follow(target, minDist, maxDist) for followers. Example: UlfketillAddsBrain does Body.Follow(npc,150,8000) in scripts/namedmobs/Midgard Named Mobs/Classic Zones/Ulfketill.cs.
- GameNPC.Formation / FormationSpacing exist, but only pet brains use them.
- The Cronker script (scripts/mobs/AlbionMobs/Cronker.cs) groups helper mobs by PackageID ('CronkerBaf') and adds them to the leader's aggro list.
- No envoy, convoy or escort class or brain exists anywhere in GameServer (searched scripts, ai/brain, quests, mode165).

NEW CODE NEEDED, for example DOL.GS.UnseelieEnvoy : GameNPC plus DOL.AI.Brain.UnseelieEnvoyBrain : StandardMobBrain, and UnseelieConvoyFollowerBrain:
- The envoy row: ClassType 'DOL.GS.UnseelieEnvoy', Brain 'DOL.AI.Brain.UnseelieEnvoyBrain', PathID 'true165_unseelie_envoy_convoy' (new Path, PathType 2, RegionID 200, points A..D around Innis; WaitTime at A = rest, at D = short stop).
- The escort and stallion rows: PackageID 'UnseelieEnvoyConvoy', RoamingRange 0. On AddToWorld (or each think), the leader finds them by PackageID within range or spawns them from templates 60165982 / 60166634.
- Followers: when not in combat, Follow(envoy, ~150, ~8000) in a fixed offset slot. Every member uses the envoy's speed.
- Shared aggro: when any member aggroes, add the target to every member's aggro list.
- Leash about 8-10k from the point where combat started, so a chase into Innis is possible (period). Then return to the path and resume at the nearest PathPoint. Before moving on, the leader waits until its followers are within about 500.
- Group respawn as described under RESPAWN.
- Fix the stallion model (2132 -> 414).

monsters.script:
PARENT ENCOUNTER: greater anglator lure ambush, Caillte Garran. This monster is the anglator's bait and does not exist on its own.

PERIOD EVIDENCE:
(a) SI Prima, Caillte Garran table (l.28740-28820): forest grazer calf 0, lesser sylvanshade 0, nosy cniogcrag 0, sporite 0, greater angler 33-34, lesser angler 19-22. Faction table: 'Predators of Hy Brasil = Lesser and Greater Angler'.
(b) SI Prima tip 'Fishing with the Greater Angler' (l.29047-29061): the greater angler is a lizard that uses a 'lure' MOB to bait players into a stronger fight. 'If the lure is close to your level, the lizard can con as much as three colors higher.' Kill the lure only with healing and endurance in reserve.
(c) SI Prima Domnann 'Enhanced Monster AI' (l.28591-28595): anglers hide from players. They use a bait creature, generally something that looks like a lower-level monster from the same zone. 'When they attack, they reveal themselves, and the lure dies.'
(d) ZAM Lesser Sylvanshade cmob=4185 (Wayback 2003-04-25, updated 2003-01-08): 'Level 0 in Vale, Rock, and Caillte; Levels 0-1 in Domnann'. ZAM Forest Grazer Calf cmob=4336 (2003-01-24) lists Domnann, VR, CG and VoB. The Midgard copies (cmob=4790/4801, 2003-01-08) are L0 in Mid SI zones that have no grazers or sylvanshades, so the L0 copies are generic lure templates.
(e) Freddyshouse 'Invisible Mob?' (2003-02-26 to 03-02): 'when you attack the sylvan it falls down and dies without beeing hit and the beckoner or anglator pops'. The anglators were 'ment to come out of stealth and run at you'; staying invisible, and /assist or F8 failing, were bugs. Another post says it 'looks more like a dinosaur'.
(f) Freddyshouse 'Should I buy DAoC' (2003-03-28): 'angler' monsters use lower-level monsters as bait, then appear from nowhere to pounce.
(g) Freddyshouse 'Hunting Grounds' (2003-08-09): a bait animal 'goes down in 2 hits' and a similar-con monster attacks.
(h) Warcry 1.62a notes (2003-04-27): 'Lesser anglators should no longer attack you while invisible.'
(i) ZAM Greater Angler cmob=5534 (2003-09-14, updated 2003-01-08): 'This monster uses a lure so beware!', Reptile 33-34. Its comment of 2003-06-06 says it 'jumped my chanter pet', unseen. The 1.56C notes (Freddyshouse 2002-11-28) renamed every Hy Brasil 'angler' to 'anglator'. ZAM quest 667 comment (2003-10-14): 'They are actually called Greater Anglators'.

BEHAVIOUR SPEC:
1. The spawn is a visible lure, this row: L0, aggro 0, no loot, no XP. A hidden 'greater anglator' sits 150-300 units away. Suggested anglator: L33-34, Reptile, model 857 ('Anglich' in the 1.64 client = the angler lizard), faction Predators of Hy Brasil. While hidden it has aggro 0, so it never ambushes passers-by.
2. Trigger: the first hostile action against the lure, from a player, pet or bot (melee swing, spell or arrow, hit or miss). The anglator reveals itself (clears STEALTH, or is spawned if the hidden-spawn variant is used) and takes the attacker plus their group as its aggro targets. It must be visible before its first swing (1.62a fix).
3. In the same tick the lure dies without taking a hit: Die with no killer credit, no XP and no loot (evidence e, g).
4. If the hidden anglator takes AoE damage, it also reveals and aggros (players used PBAE/GTAE, evidence e).
5. When the anglator resets alive (leaves aggro and returns home), it re-stealths and its lure respawns. When the anglator dies, any living lure is removed, and both respawn together on the anglator's respawn timer.
6. The lure's look is one of the zone's L0 lure pool: forest grazer calf, lesser sylvanshade, nosy cniogcrag or sporite (evidence a). Either fixed per row (this row = calf) or picked at random on each respawn.
7. Do not reproduce the 2003 bugs: stay targetable with F8 and /assist after revealing.

ALREADY IN THE SERVER:
- GameNPC.eFlags.STEALTH (0x02).
- StandardMobState_AGGRO.Enter clears STEALTH, and Exit re-applies it if WasStealthed (ai/brain/StandardMob/StandardMobState.cs l.97-112).
- mode165/StealthedMonsters165.cs: a stealthed monster is invisible beyond max(150, aggro range), with the same rule for players and bots.
- Closest existing pattern: DOL.GS.UrchinAmbusher : StealtherMob (scripts/mobs/AlbionMobs/UrchinAmbusher.cs) with UrchinAmbusherBrain.OnAttackedByEnemy -> LeaveStealth (ai/brain/Special/UrchinAmbusherBrain.cs).

NO ANGLATOR OR LURE CODE EXISTS. A grep for anglator/lure finds nothing; the only 'angler' hits are Strangler/Tangler. New code needed:
(1) DOL.GS.Anglator : StealtherMob + AnglatorBrain : StandardMobBrain. AddToWorld spawns or links its lure, and it exposes Trigger(attacker).
(2) DOL.GS.AnglatorLure : GameNPC. Override OnAttackedByEnemy/TakeDamage to call owner.Trigger(attacker), then Die without XP or loot.
(3) Linking: either the anglator row spawns its lure from NpcTemplate 60161028 at an offset (then this row becomes the anglator's spawn point), or the lure row keeps ClassType 'DOL.GS.AnglatorLure' and finds the nearest Anglator within 400 units. Simpler variant with no stealth rendering: only the lure row exists, and on trigger it spawns a greater anglator 150-250 units away that attacks at once. The spawned anglator despawns about 60 s after leaving combat, and then the lure respawns.
The greater anglator itself has no row or template yet. It needs its own placement at this spot: Prima callout '3 GREAT ANGLER'.

Part of the greater anglator lure ambush; see the forest grazer calf entry for the full spec and evidence. Sylvanshade-specific evidence:
- ZAM Lesser Sylvanshade cmob=4185 (Wayback 2003-04-25, updated 2003-01-08): 'Level 0 in Vale, Rock, and Caillte; Levels 0-1 in Domnann'.
- ZAM Midgard Lesser Sylvanshade cmob=4801 (2003-01-08; comment 2003-04-16 'this is a hib mob in SI zone') is L0 in Aegir's Landing, Gripklosa, Munin Sound and Faraheim, zones with no real sylvanshades. That shows the L0 copy is a generic lure template.
- Freddyshouse 2003-02-26 (World's End): anglators 'are linked to the dusky sylvan shades'. 'When you attack the sylvan it falls down and dies without beeing hit and the beckoner or anglator pops.' This is the exact lure behaviour, with a sylvanshade-type lure.
- SI Prima Domnann AI (l.28591-28595): 'When they attack, they reveal themselves, and the lure dies.'

Spec, identical to the calf:
1. This row is a visible L0 lure, aggro 0, with no loot and no XP. A hidden greater anglator (L33-34, Reptile, suggested model 857 'Anglich') waits 150-300 units away with aggro 0.
2. The first hostile action on the lure, by a player, pet or bot, reveals the anglator before it swings (Warcry 1.62a) and gives it the attacker and their group as targets. The lure dies at once without giving credit.
3. AoE damage on the hidden anglator also reveals it.
4. When the anglator resets, it re-stealths and the lure respawns. On the anglator's death and respawn, the lure comes back with it.
5. Stay targetable with F8 and /assist (the 2003 bugs are not to be copied).

Existing server pieces: eFlags.STEALTH, StandardMobState_AGGRO stealth handling, mode165/StealthedMonsters165.cs, and the UrchinAmbusher/UrchinAmbusherBrain pattern. New code needed: Anglator : StealtherMob + AnglatorBrain, AnglatorLure : GameNPC (on attack: owner.Trigger(attacker), then Die with no XP or loot), and the lure-anglator link, or the simpler variant where the lure spawns the anglator on trigger. monsters.script:
PERIOD EVIDENCE OF A SCRIPT: NONE FOUND. Searched: all three Prima guides (the only mentions are the Atlas map label and loot line, Atlas txt lines 18531/19097); Allakhazam's Lough Gur bestiary (139 creatures, every era, and Earl Gerald, Aine and Bodb are absent); every period Allakhazam mob/item/quest/zone page and comment in the archive; Wayback Warcry; Freddyshouse 2001-2004 (full crawl); CapnBry (no zone 204 data); Uthgard; web search. No source names a trigger, adds, timer, patrol, despawn or special attack for any of the three. Do NOT invent one as 'period'.

WHAT THE PERIOD SOURCES DO SHOW: (1) The Atlas (2002) puts the three on the lake island together with the little unicorns, and Earl Gerald shares Aine's loot table. (2) Low-level players visited that island freely in 2002: Freddyshouse 2002-09-17, 'I love the Faerie horses on that island near Innis... sometimes I just swim over there to watch them'; 2002-10-21, the island suggested as a memorial site. No post anywhere mentions a level 60+ named there. So the three were either non-aggressive or not normally up. A non-aggressive static named mob is the reading that contradicts no source.

SPEC (no new code needed): a plain DOL.GS.GameNPC spawn row, ClassType 'DOL.GS.GameNPC', Brain empty (StandardMobBrain). AggroLevel 0, RoamingRange 0, RespawnInterval 3600 s. FactionID 0. BAF note: in this server a faction-less mob brings only faction-less mobs of the SAME name (ai/brain/StandardMob/BafFriends.cs). Earl Gerald, Bodb and Aine therefore will not assist each other, and they will not pull the faerie horses or little unicorns. Giving the three a shared faction would make them assist each other, but no period source says they did, so leave it off. Loot: MobXLootTemplate rows under the name 'Earl Gerald' pointing at the same loot template as Aine.

ALREADY IN THE SERVER: no class or brain for Earl Gerald, Aine, Bodb or any Lough Gur legend (grep of GameServer scripts/, namedmobs/, ai/brain/, quests/, mode165/ found only bot first-name lists). Reusable only if the owner explicitly asks for a legend-inspired, NON-period timing: DOL.GS.NightSpawn / DOL.GS.DaySpawn (scripts/mobs/TimeDependentSpawnNpc.cs). Those classes hide the NPC (model 1, PEACE/CANTTARGET) outside its time window, and the row just sets ClassType 'DOL.GS.NightSpawn'. Folklore (not a DAoC source) says Earl Gerald rides around the lake every seven years on a silver-shod white horse. Any 'rare appearance' mechanic would be invented, so it is an owner decision and not part of this spec. Not recommended: GameEpicBoss (the MelancholicFairyQueen base) with custom resists or HP, since nothing period supports boss mechanics here.

monsters.script:
NO existing script or brain implements Arr. I searched scripts/namedmobs, ai/brain, mode165 and quests for Arr, griffon snatch and swoop: nothing. New code is needed, e.g. class DOL.GS.Arr : GameEpicBoss (or GameNPC) with brain DOL.AI.Brain.ArrBrain : StandardMobBrain. The spawn row references it with ClassType='DOL.GS.Arr' and Brain='' (set the brain in AddToWorld, like Hurika), or ClassType GameNPC plus Brain='DOL.AI.Brain.ArrBrain'.

REUSABLE SERVER CODE: (a) scripts/namedmobs/TuscarianGlacier/TorstAndHurika.cs, Hurika/HurikaBrain: a named griffon with a waypoint flying patrol (HurikaFlyingPath with WalkTo between Point3Ds while not in combat), the FLYING flag cleared when it closes to melee and restored on reset, a FightIsOver reset, and a gust that MoveTo's a random player up into the air. (b) spells/Masterlevel/Sojourner.cs FZSpellHandler with ai/brain/ZephyrBrain.cs: a working 'pick a player up and carry him' mechanic. The carrier NPC follows the target; on arrival the target gets IsStunned=true, SpellFumbleChance+100, StopAttack/StopCurrentSpellcast and player.MountSteed(npc,true); the NPC then WalkTo's a destination; on expiry DismountSteed(true), the debuffs are removed and Out.SendUpdateMaxSpeed() is sent. Reuse this pattern, with Arr himself (or a hidden carrier NPC that Arr follows) as the steed. POLICY CONFLICT: scripts/namedmobs/EpicEncounterMechanics.cs sets AllowDisplacement => false ('Bot raids cannot recover safely from scripted jail/air teleports') and AllowGlacierGriffonPatrol => false. Arr's whole period identity is a displacement, so the owner must approve a separate flag (e.g. AllowArrSnatch) or the current policy will disable it. Recommendation: snatch only GamePlayer, or make bots/companions re-path back to the group after a drop.

1) PATROL (Prima SI p.121 'patrols the frigid mountains of Gripklosa'; p.123 tip 'Should his sights settle on you'): while out of combat, fly a loop with FLYING (Flags 32) at roughly 10000-10500 Z. The highest navmesh ground on the route is 9020, so this keeps him out of reach. Loop the waypoints back and forth, in world coords: W1 (288528,285760) = local 10K,40K (Allakhazam 2003-07-25 sighting); W2 (297628,287760) = Prima map marker 1 (spawn); W3 (314528,286760) = mid-line; W4 (330928,286560) = local 52.4,40.8 (Illia loc, post-2003 text); optional W5 (340528,263760) = toward the NW corner of Delling Crater (Allakhazam 2003-07-03 eyewitness, approximate). The radar has no data, so the path joins the only evidence points, all on local y = 40-42K. Freddyshouse 2003-12-09 (quoting daoc-trophy-mobs): 'there's no way to attack him. You have to visit areas ... where Arr is known to fly and wait for him to attack you'. Allakhazam 2003-07-03: 'Arr just appeared out of nowhere on us'. So while patrolling, Arr must not be attackable or pullable: add CANTTARGET (8) and optionally DONTSHOWNAME (4) during patrol, and remove them when he swoops.

2) TRIGGER/AGGRO: Aggro Chance High (Allakhazam). Pick a living player (or bot) below him within a wide horizontal radius (no period number; suggest about 1500-2000 XY because he is airborne) as the snatch target.

3) SWOOP AND SNATCH (Prima SI p.121: 'swoops down to pick up adventurers with its claws, only to drop them to their deaths'; p.123 tip: 'he'll snatch you up in his talons and take you to a nearby nest to handle you one-on-one'; Illia description, by 2003-06-30: 'Arr's swoop and drop somewhere else attack ... Once you release it is impossible to get back to gravestone on foot'): dive to the target. On contact, run the Zephyr pickup (stun, fumble, MountSteed). Fly at carry speed (Zephyr uses 400; no period figure) to the NEST and dismount the player there. No period source gives a nest location; it must be a spot unreachable on foot (Illia). Terrain-derived suggestion, not period: an unwalkable summit patch next to marker 1 at local (22400,38900) = world (300928,284660), heightmap Z about 9150 (terrain.pcx*8 + offset.pcx*48, no navmesh floor there; peak cell (22144,38272) is 9408). After the drop, Arr lands (clear FLYING) and melees the victim one-on-one (Prima). Optional: release him from higher up so fall damage applies ('drop them to their deaths'). GamePlayer.CalcFallDamage exists but is client-driven and leaves 1 HP, so the kill comes from Arr's melee. Melee is Slash. Allakhazam 2004-01-21, post-period but indicative: hits of 384 before absorb, two-shotting a player.

4) FIGHT: Prima says 'a large group of level 40+ players is needed' and 'chances decrease if he attacks your Healers first. Having a tank with a good taunt helps keep your Healers alive'. So Arr must stay tauntable and use normal hate; no healer-targeting rule is stated, so do not add one. When the snatched victim dies, or a group engages him on the ground, he fights normally and can be attacked. Repeating the snatch during combat is implied by 'swoop and drop ... attack' (Illia) but has no period timer; if wanted, use Hurika's 15-20 s random timer as a server precedent and mark it non-period.

5) RESET/DESPAWN: no adds, no health-% phases, no time-of-day or quest trigger in any period source. On FightIsOver (8 s quiet, EpicEncounterMechanics.FightIsOver): full health, restore FLYING plus the no-target flags, resume the patrol. Do NOT implement the 2004-01-21 Allakhazam report of a player 'teleported back to the scene of the crime' after respawning at bind; it is post-period and reads as a bug.

6) DEATH: normal loot (see notes); respawn by the SI-epic respawn property. Not linked to the avalanche: Allakhazam 2007 comment 'Arr is not related to the Avalanche in any way', against a 2004 rumour.

monsters.script:
ENCOUNTER: Ogres vs. Orc Battle (parent = Thergus the Inspirer; this mob leads each ogre squad).

PERIOD EVIDENCE
(a) Prima SI 2002, Aldland 'The Right Place at the Right Time': Thergus gives a long speech; a bunch of ogres gather; when he concludes, 'the ogres gather in formation and march to battle'. Halfway down the western coastline they meet an Orc coast guard squad and a battle ensues.
(b) Freddyshouse 'new SI zone in 1.65a', grebneklaf 2003-08-23 (reposted 2003-08-29): the event starts outside Krondon. A broadcast by 'an Ogre speaker' says humans deserted the ogres, so they will fend for themselves; they learned from humans that access to water gives power; the orcs stand between the ogres and the water, so they will remove them. Then 'some Ogres patrols form up, 4 or 5 teams, about 10 Ogres in each team with an Ogre squadleader in each'. They head for the water, where orc coastguards (not finguards) have teamed up, and fight. 'Ogres gets badly creamed'.
(c) Freddyshouse 'Liz the troublemaker', Eliz 2003-02-26: at the west coast both forces stood with 'formations ready', glaring and taunting at each other, and did not start. A friend said 'they would only fight at certain times'. She rooted one ogre: 'the entire Ogre army stormed towards me', the orcs (who liked her) engaged, and a 'massive brawl' followed.
(d) Freddyshouse 2003-05-28/29: pcentella says 'a crazy guildie pulled the groups of ogres towards the neutral orcs, so we helped the orcs win'. In the same thread loxleyhood says the Colialt event 'happens on random nights'.
(e) Larik 2003-08-28: 'orc/ogre armies ... never seen them do anything but stand around looking at each other'.
(f) Brannor 2003-02-04: 'Orcs and Ogres at war with each other - I walked into the middle of a small war'.
(g) mestoph 2003-06-05 and 06-08: 'hit the coast from diogel (ogres vs orcs bit)'; 'Orcs vs Ogres battle (Beach near Diogel)' is a mini-event with high unique-drop rates.

SPEC
1) STANDBY (permanent, DB rows): 1 squad leader at (367050,503640,3280) h0, as Prima drew it, plus its squad of 9 'thrawn ogre thresher' (existing NpcTemplate 60167050, lv44-48, faction 8) standing in a 3x3 block behind it (north) at about 120 spacing, all heading 0, roaming 0. Prima's 'THRAWN OGRE THRESHER' label is 1200 north at (367050,502440,3283), on the same flat ridge at Z~3280. The squad links: when any member is attacked, all members aggro the attacker. That is period (c), and existing BafFriends / StandardMobBrain BAF mostly covers it; add the squad-wide AddAggroListTo like CronkerBrain does. Their 500 aggro range keeps them out of reach of the orc camp at (367019,506762) until the event or a player pull. Then StandardMobBrain.CheckNpcAggro / CanAggroTarget already makes faction-8 ogres attack faction-37 orcs: orc coastal sergeant template 60164683 and orc coast guard template 60164682 are both FactionID 37 with ReplaceMobValues=1. So a player pull into the orcs starts the brawl with no new code, which is periods (c) and (d).
2) TRIGGER: the period says only 'at certain times' / not every time. The interval is not sourced; owner choice, for example a game-time check like CronkerBrain (WorldMgr.GetCurrentGameTime) once per few real hours, with a random skip, and only if a player is in Aldland. Thergus starts it (see his entry).
3) SPEECH: Thergus broadcasts to players within about 3000-5000 of the Outerward for about 1-2 minutes; the AmminusPilus/HighPriestAndania BroadcastMessage pattern exists. No recorded period text survives, only the grebneklaf paraphrase in (b). Lines must be flagged as reconstructed, and the owner must approve them under the dialogue rule.
4) FORM UP: when the speech ends, spawn 4 squads (period '4 or 5'). Each is 1 thrawn ogre squad leader + 9 thrawn ogre threshers ('about 10 Ogres in each team'), RespawnInterval -1 / temporary. Leader slots at the west edge of the Outerward crowd: (384800,482100,3137), (384800,482700,3159), (384300,482100,3118), (384300,482700,3162), and a 5th if wanted at (383800,482400,3152). Threshers form up behind each leader. The existing GameNPC.Formation / FormationSpacing fields exist but are only wired for Bonedancer pets, so this needs new follower code: each thresher follows its leader at an offset.
5) MARCH: the leaders walk in column at walk speed (not 191 run) along this navmesh route, which avoids the mountains a straight line would cross (Z up to 6000): (386500,483250,3116) -> (384500,482500,3143) -> (382500,482500,3096) -> (380500,482500,3082) -> (378500,482500,3082) -> (376500,483750,3082) -> (374500,485750,3173) -> (372500,487750,3204) -> (370500,489750,3183) -> (370500,491750,3130) -> (370250,493750,3155) -> (369750,495750,3104) -> (368000,497750,3080) -> (367000,499750,3064) -> (367000,501750,3276) -> battle line about (366800-368300, 503000, Z 3282-3272). The route passes the existing 14-thresher group at (373.9k,481.9k), which is faction 8 and friendly. Region 51 has no PathPoints, so either insert a Path/PathPoints row and use MoveOnPath, or use PathTo through PathfindingProvider. While marching, set AggroRange 0 or suppress NPC aggro. Otherwise faction-8 ogres will attack faction-16 lammia, griffins, serpents and sea hounds near the coast route and break up. Players can still attack them.
6) STAND OFF then CHARGE: line up beside the standby squad facing south (h0) and hold about 2-5 minutes ('glaring at eachother, and taunting', period (c)). Then all ogre squads, standby included, walk south to the orc camp. Existing faction aggro (8 vs 37) does the fighting. Do not touch any combat numbers; the period result was 'Ogres gets badly creamed'.
7) END: the event is over when every event ogre is dead, or after a timeout (for example 15 minutes). Survivors despawn (or walk back and despawn), and the event can fire again after the cycle timer. Standby rows respawn normally (80 s like the live thrawn rows), or wait until the event is idle.
8) LOOT: as in notes (Squad-leader's Shield; owner sets the chance).

ALREADY IN THE SERVER: faction war (LinkedFaction 8<->37 hostile; StandardMobBrain.CanAggroTarget EnemyFactions), BAF, game-time checks (CronkerBrain pattern), broadcast helpers, PathTo/MoveOnPath, and the navmesh for zone 56.
NEEDS NEW CODE: an event controller (new ClassType, for example DOL.GS.Scripts.ThergusTheInspirer + ThergusBrain), squad/formation follower logic, march-time aggro suppression, the timed stand-off and charge, cleanup, and a LootTemplate row. There is no existing script for any part of this encounter: I grepped scripts\namedmobs, scripts, ai\brain, quests and mode165 for thergus / squad / thrawn. The Krondon scripts (DebenSeGecynde.cs) are dungeon bosses and unrelated.

monsters.script:
Controller for the Ogres vs. Orc Battle (see the Thrawn Ogre Squad-Leader entry for the full spec). Summary:
(1) Idle by the Outerward crowd.
(2) At the event time (period: 'only fight at certain times', Eliz/Freddyshouse 2003-02-26; interval not sourced), broadcast the speech to nearby players for 1-2 minutes. Prima: 'a long inspirational speech'; content paraphrased by grebneklaf 2003-08-23.
(3) At the end, spawn 4 (or 5) squads of 1 thrawn ogre squad leader + 9 thrawn ogre threshers at (384800,482100), (384800,482700), (384300,482100), (384300,482700), (383800,482400). Prima: 'the ogres gather in formation and march to battle'; grebneklaf: '4 or 5 teams, about 10 Ogres in each team with an Ogre squadleader in each'.
(4) March them along the navmesh route to the coast battle line at about y 503000.
(5) Hold, then charge the orc coastal sergeants and coast guards at (367019,506762). Existing faction 8 vs 37 aggro does the fighting.
(6) Clean up after all event ogres die or a timeout, then re-arm the cycle.
New code: ClassType for example DOL.GS.Scripts.ThergusTheInspirer with Brain ThergusBrain (StandardMobBrain subclass, game-time check like CronkerBrain). The spawn row references it via Mob.ClassType + Mob.Brain. Nothing exists in the server today.

There is no CapnBry radar for zone 50, no Uthgard dot, and no Prima/Kirstena label (the SI Prima Avalon City map p.93 marks only 'A' and Xanxicar). I found the lair and its tunnels in our world from the navmesh and the live rows: Sys'sro 20563 at 41505,39496,8040; 6 SyssroBaf alblasters and 2 dragoons around the guagaran pit (pit floor about Z 7700); lair floor Z 8024-8064. The SW tunnel is the shortest way in from the zone entrance (31159,47380, the bot nav entry for Sys'sro). It runs: ramp down at 37500,42900 (veteran/alblaster camp, Z 8250 to 8170), then a corridor, then a small room at 39000,43250 (veteran 20493, alblaster 20494), then alblaster 20495 at 40050,43149. From there a straight corridor runs north (x 39950-40100, floor 8027) into the lair's SW corner, where dragoons 20497/20499/20555 stand at y 42300. The spawn is the middle of that last corridor. Z checked with K.ground = 8027, an exact navmesh floor. There is also a north approach (round room with veterans at 41239,36752, then the east loop to the lair's SE side). If the owner prefers that tunnel, the other choice is its corridor near 43200,38250, but nothing in the period sources favours it.
monsters.script:
PERIOD EVIDENCE: (1) Allakhazam cmob 5650, 'Call for help...', Jun 02 2003: it is in the tunnel leading into the main part of the AC sewers (Sys'sro's lair). If left alive it runs into the lair and calls for help ('can be nasty'). (2) Allakhazam cmob 5671 (Sys'sro), 'Killing Sys'ro', May 23 2003: on the way in, if a scout spots you and runs for Sys'sro, mez the scout or run out and zone, because everything for miles around will aggro you. So the scout is stopped by mez, its trigger is being spotted, and the alarm is wide. The same post says archers respawn during the fight. (3) SI Prima p.93 Avalon City monster list: 'panicked syhr'phint 50' (level only, no text). (4) Freddyshouse 'To Anyone Planning Epic Raids In Albion' (2003-02-27): Sys'sro is the easiest AC boss if you 'don't aggro adds', clearing his area first helps, and he throws players into the pit. NEW CODE NEEDED: a brain DOL.AI.Brain.PanickedSyhrphintBrain : StandardMobBrain. Best place is next to Sys'sro in SyssroTheRuthless.cs. The DB row is ClassType DOL.GS.GameNPC, Brain 'DOL.AI.Brain.PanickedSyhrphintBrain', PackageID NOT 'SyssroBaf' (otherwise Sys'sro's own baf would drag it in), e.g. 'Public_DB'. Faction 11, AggroLevel 200, AggroRange 500. Behaviour:
(a) IDLE at spawn facing south (heading 0), toward players coming up from alblaster 20495.
(b) TRIGGER: a player or player pet comes within aggro range with LOS (the period word is 'spots you'), or it is attacked. On trigger it records its aggro list (the spotter, plus that player's group, the way DOL bafs normally add a group) and does NOT fight. It switches to FLEE: run at max speed, using pathing (PathTo/WalkTo with navmesh), to a point in front of Sys'sro, 41100,39700,8024. The route is the corridor north (40025,42300), then the lair's west rim (40300,41800 to 40300,39900), then 41100,39700, about 3,700 units, roughly 20 s at speed 180. Damage taken while fleeing does NOT cancel the run (period: 'if allowed to live'). Mez, stun or root stop it naturally (period counter is 'mez the scout'), and it continues the run when the effect ends. If it dies before arriving, nothing happens.
(c) ALARM, on arriving within about 300 of the destination or about 600 of Sys'sro. Add its aggro list to: Sys'sro's brain (this also fires the existing SyssroBaf pull); every live PackageID 'SyssroBaf' NPC; and, because the period says 'everything for miles around', every live faction-11 NPC in the lair room (X 39750-43000, Y 38500-42750, Z 7900-8150). That room includes dragoons 20521/20576/20497/20499/20555. Leave PitMonsters out: they do not move and only aggro in melee range. Do it once per trigger. A one-line system message to the spotted players is fine (e.g. '<name> runs into the lair, crying for help!'). It is a server convention like ScoutMobBrain's 'is alerted by your presence'. No period quote exists, so do not present one as period text.
(d) After the alarm it fights as a normal level-50 syhr'phint (StandardMobBrain). The period does not say; this is the least invented choice.
(e) RESET: when its aggro list empties, RETURN_TO_SPAWN and re-arm.
(f) RESPAWN: 180 s, as the syhr'phint family. Respawns during a raid fit the period (May 2003 post: 'kill any respawned archers').
No timers or health-% adds: the period sources describe none. Loot: none known, family coin only.
Related, not this monster: Prima lists 'sys'sro checker' (level 0) and 'starving trained guagaran' (59) / 'trained guagaran' in AC. The server's pit monsters are a scripted stand-in called 'Sys'sro's Pit Monster'. The checker is probably an invisible encounter helper, but no source says what it does.

THIS MONSTER'S ROLE: Celain's permanent pet, the 'Zombie Lieutenant'. It appears with him and follows him (Allakhazam 3377, 12 Nov 2002: 'he has a Zombie Lieutenant (green)'; 23 Nov 2003 comment, 3 weeks after the cutoff: 'He appeared with a buddy ... crony was grey').
1) TRIGGER/TIMING: Celain appears at 09:00 game time ('Spawned for me at exactly 9am', Allakhazam Secret Orders, 17 Jul 2003; 'Celain Spawned at 9h00 as others have stated', 23 Nov 2003). When he despawns is not recorded, so keep him up until he is killed and bring him back at the next 09:00. The lieutenant appears with him at his side.
2) PET: follows Celain at about 120 units and fights whatever Celain fights, both ways.
3) RAISES (the other five names, see their entries): while Celain is alive and out of combat, every T seconds he raises one more undead (undead armswoman, cleric, mercenary, paladin, paladin lieutenant) 150-300 units from himself, up to a cap. Period: 'if left long enough he will raise more undead and they will add if you attack him near them' (Allakhazam 3377, 12 Nov 2002). T and the cap are NOT in any period source; they are tunables (suggest T = 60-120 s and a cap of 5, one of each type, so the full group is the six names Illia logged). He does not raise while in combat ('left long enough').
4) ASSIST: if Celain, the lieutenant or a raised undead is attacked, every member within about 1000 units joins in.
5) DEATH/DESPAWN: no period data. Suggest raised undead despawn 10 min after Celain dies, or when they reset out of combat. The lieutenant goes away with Celain and returns with him at 09:00.
6) LOOT: none for all six (Prima '(no loot)'; Illia 'Has No Loot'). Normal XP.

Implement it with a Mob row where Brain='DOL.AI.Brain.QuestFellowBrain', plus classic-quests.json 'Fellows': {'<this Mob_ID>': 'Celain Eirich'} (the leader is looked up by name in the same region and realm, within 6000; this is how Fjall's fenrir shredders work). monsters.script:
GORMROR'S RAID ON DYRFJELL (parent encounter: Gormror + 4 lieutenants + about 30 morvalt adds + disease clouds).
PERIOD EVIDENCE:
(1) Prima SI Aegir's Landing encounters (p.118, txt l.15979-15986): Gormror is 'a creature with the ability to inspire the masses of morvalts in the region to attack the nearby town of Dyrfjell'. It takes a couple of groups 'because the guards need help with this one'. 'Do not fret if you lose, as they leave the village intact to raid another day.'
(2) Prima SI Enhanced Monster AI (l.15994): 'watch for an attack by the Formorians where they hurl disease into the town.'
(3) 1.62 notes (Freddyshouse 2003-05-20): 'The Morvalt that join Gormor and his lieutenants in their disease attack on Dyrfjell will no longer linger outside of the town after their leaders have left or been killed.'
(4) frols, 2003-08-16: 'cloud thingies' at different places in town, entering one diseases you; outside were about 100 morvalts with 8 commanders; 'he kept spamming all races will die'; after killing them all 'the clouds stopped'.
(5) Roo, 2003-08-16: an NPC outside town throws rotten meat into the town; kill him and the disease clouds stop until he respawns.
(6) kjel, 2003-08-18: 'a scripted event that came with SI, randomly happens'.

NEW CODE (proposed): class DOL.GS.Scripts.Gormror165 : GameNPC with brain GormrorRaidBrain : StandardMobBrain set in AddToWorld (Mob.ClassType='DOL.GS.Scripts.Gormror165', Brain column empty). Also class GormrorDisease165 : GameNPC for the clouds.
SEQUENCE:
a) IDLE: Gormror is hidden at 277037,330107 (TimeDependentSpawnNpc-style flags). A random timer starts the raid (period: 'randomly happens'; no interval is recorded, so the owner picks one, e.g. 60-180 min).

The road needs a walk test in game: the region has no navmesh. Lieutenants and adds follow in formation. While marching or fighting, Gormror yells 'All races will die!' (frols) as ambient 'roaming'/'aggroing'.
d) DISEASE: when the raid reaches the town, or from the start of the raid (period: the meat is thrown from outside town), spawn N GormrorDisease165 clouds (lvl 99, PEACE + CANTTARGET + DONTSHOWNAME, suggested model 941 'CorrosiveCloud' from the 1.64 list) at random picks from the 27 radar spots below. Each cloud pulses an existing Disease spell (e.g. SpellID 61028 'Disease', 60 s) on players inside a small radius (design value, e.g. 150). e) GUARDS: during the raid, raiders must attack the Dyrfjell guards and the guards must fight back (Prima: 'the guards need help'). Either give raiders a CheckNpcAggro that targets realm-2 guards within range, or switch the town guards to GuardBrain while the raid lasts.

monsters.script:
TALVOR -> TALVOR'S SPIRIT (on-death successor).
PERIOD EVIDENCE:
- Prima SI, Aegir's Landing 'Round Two, FIGHT!' (txt l.15970-15976): Talvor 'looks easy at first glance. But once slain, his spirit rises up to seek revenge upon his killers. You need a group of level 10-15 to put him down for good. Keep a healer on your main tank'.
- Illia/Allakhazam Talvor's Spirit page (updated 2003-07-09, captured 2003-09-09): it 'will appear once Travor is killed'; very hard to kill; aggro High; lvl 25; loot Talvor's Staff of Bonedancing.
- Allakhazam Talvor page: 'When you kill him Talvor's Spirit will be released, be ready to fight.'
ALREADY IN THE SERVER: nothing. A grep for 'talvor' finds no script. Talvor is a plain DOL.GS.GameNPC row (Mob 100019786, lvl 22, model 840, RespawnInterval 80). Reusable patterns: Die() overrides that spawn NPCs (SisterBlythe.cs spawns FallenExecutioner with RespawnInterval=-1); a GameLivingEvent.Dying handler on one NPC (Alluvian.cs, AncestralSecrets.cs).
NEW CODE (proposed): either set Talvor's Mob.ClassType to 'DOL.GS.Scripts.Talvor165' (a GameNPC overriding Die), or add a data-driven mode165 death-successor hook (GameEventMgr GameLivingEvent.Dying, keyed on Name='Talvor' and Region=151) that other 'X rises when Y dies' encounters can reuse. Spirit class 'DOL.GS.Scripts.TalvorsSpirit165' : GameNPC with StandardMobBrain, or a plain GameNPC filled from a new NpcTemplate.
SEQUENCE:
1) Talvor dies: run his normal death and loot (Talvors_Gem). Then at once (period gives no delay; at most ~1-2 s for the visual) spawn Talvor's Spirit at Talvor's death X/Y/Z/heading. Use: level 25, model 929, size 49, BodyType 11 Undead, Race 2009, Talvor's faction/realm 0, AggroLevel and AggroRange like Talvor (200/500), speed 191, RespawnInterval -1 (never respawns by itself), PackageID 'TalvorSpirit'.
2) Revenge: copy Talvor's aggro list (his killers and the group that hit him) into the spirit's aggro list and start the attack on the top entry ('seek revenge upon his killers'). Normal undead melee; Prima names no special attacks.
3) Only one spirit may exist: skip the spawn if a live 'TalvorSpirit' NPC is within ~3000 units.
4) Despawn (design, no period figure): if the spirit has no aggro target for ~60 s, or walks more than ~2000 units from where it rose, remove it without loot.
5) Spirit death: drop loot template "talvor's spirit" (Talvors_Staff_of_Bonedancing; see notes) and coin by the server formula for lvl 25 Undead. Talvor himself respawns on his own existing 80 s timer and is unchanged.
Bots and companions: treat Talvor plus the spirit as one group-of-10-15 encounter (Prima).

monsters.script:
PARENT ENCOUNTER 'THE PROCESSION', Star Lake, Domnann. The treant sprouts below use this same spec.
PERIOD EVIDENCE: (1) Prima Shrouded Isles guide 2002, Domnann 'Right Place at the Right Time' (txt l.28624-28633): 'Every so often' a small procession of priests leaves Bann-didein and heads south along the road to the north shore of Star Lake. There they throw treant seeds into the lake, treant sprouts emerge, and the procession goes back to the grove with the sprouts. Botonids sometimes attack this peaceful ceremony, and players can help one side or the other. (2) Mythic pre-release AI notes, quoted on Freddyshouse 2002-10-30 (thread 'Monster AI', id 102638): a Sylvan procession throws magic dust into a lake, small treant seedlings sprout, it is a friendly event that Fomorian monsters 'often' attack, and players may protect it. The post-release Prima says botonids, so use botonids. (3) ZAM cmob=5848 (Wayback 2003-09-09): Central Treant Sprout, Plant, level 12-12, Domnann. Killing it lowers Outland Residents, Z'zozicck Zhxizzckrrk, Tree of Ages and The Watcher. No loot and no comments. (4) Prima Domnann level table: 'central treant sprout 12', 'treant sprout 12'. Neither is on the Prima map, which fits an event-only spawn.
ALREADY IN THE SERVER: nothing. A grep for procession, treant sprout and Star Lake in GameServer finds no code. Reusable pieces: GameNPC.PathTo/WalkTo (gameobjects/GameNPC.cs:869-884, navmesh pathing); ECSGameTimer; the invisible controller-NPC pattern in scripts/mobs/HiberniaMobs/ParthananFarm.cs (ParthananFarmController1 : GameNPC with an APlayerVicinityBrain that spawns and walks adds); RoundsBrain plus MovementMgr.LoadPath for a stored Path/PathPoints route; the hidden-NPC flags in scripts/mobs/TimeDependentSpawnNpc.cs (CANTTARGET|DONTSHOWNAME|PEACE, model 1).
NEW CODE NEEDED: a class such as DOL.GS.Scripts.StarLakeProcessionController, placed as ONE Mob row (region 181, at Bann-didein about 427068,405631,4441, invisible, ClassType = that class). It spawns and despawns every procession NPC itself, so the sprouts get no static Mob rows.
SEQUENCE: (a) Trigger: a repeating timer. Prima only says 'every so often', so the interval is unsourced; suggest a random 45-90 min of real time, configurable, not tied to day or night. Start one only when none is running and a player is within about 6000 of the route, to stay light. (b) Spawn the priests at Bann-didein (427068,405631,4441). Prima says only 'a small procession of priests', so the default of 3 is unsourced. Probable identity: 'Priestess of the Watch' (ZAM cmob=13631: NPC, Crush, level 19-20, habitat 'Domnann (Nerar Bann Didein)'; that page's last update is 2008, so it is not period-proven). Our DB has template 60165023 (Sylvan female model 745, level 19, Realm 3) and one static row, 100028768. The sprouts' 'The Watcher' faction supports the link. Give the priests faction 111. (c) Walk at walking pace (about 100, a choice) with PathTo through the horse road 'south along the road': (427314,407336,4483), then (427695,410923,4479). Then go cross-country southeast: (432600,414050,4470), (436030,416255,4427). The ritual line on the north shore is (437750,416700,4340), (438000,416650,4342) and (438250,416700,4328), heading 0, facing the lake. (d) Ritual: the priests emote or cast a visual 'throw seeds' effect. About 10-20 s later, spawn on the water 1 central treant sprout at (438000,417550,4131), heading 2048, plus the treant sprouts (see that entry; the default of 4 is unsourced). The sprouts walk to the shore (438000,417050,4220) and fall in with the central sprout at the middle of the column. (e) Return: the whole group walks the route back in reverse to Bann-didein and despawns there. Prima says 'back to the grove'; Bann-didein is the default because it is the only named origin. The owner's alternative is the Grove of Domnann (423482,442382,5952) along the horse road at X about 422k. Then reschedule. Despawn everything if the group has been stuck for more than 10 min. (f) Attack: Prima says 'may sometimes be attacked by botonids'. A chance per procession of about 1 in 3 is unsourced. The best attacker candidate is 'botonid displacer'. Prima lists it in Domnann at level 20 but not on the map; ZAM cmob=5846 (Wayback 2003-09-16) has it as Insect level 20, lowering Botonids. It has NO rows in our DB, so it is probably event-only, but that link is an inference. Fallback: existing spiky botonids (13-16) or botonid leaves (9-11). Use model 818 and faction 69 (Botonids). Spawn 2-3 of them about 1500 units from the ritual point and force aggro onto the sprouts and priests. Do not rely on factions: 69 is linked hostile only to 98 Outland Residents and 89, not directly to 111. Players may kill either side. The sprouts and displacers are Realm 0 and attackable; the priests stay Realm 3 like the DB row. (g) Sprouts: AggroLevel 0 and they fight back when hit. If all sprouts die, the priests still go home. No loot (ZAM loot list empty); coin follows the Plant body type.
STATS: level 12 (Prima and ZAM), BodyType 10 Plant, FactionID 111 The Watcher (it lowers Watcher, Tree of Ages, Outland Residents and Z'zozicck, which are all 111 or its friends in LinkedFaction), Realm 0.

monsters.script:
LURE AMBUSH. Do NOT insert new scourgin rows. Change these 13 existing botonid seedling Mob rows so that ClassType = 'DOL.GS.Scripts.BotonidSeedling' (Brain column empty; the script sets its own brain). Label A: 100027648, 100023803, 100026139, 100027977, 100026023, 100025572, 100027727, 100023379, 100024847. Label B: 100025444, 100024407, 100024326, 100026130. The other 77 seedlings stay plain GameNPC.
PERIOD EVIDENCE: Prima SI 2002, Domnann 'Enhanced Monster AI' (txt l.28585-28589): scourgin and Domnann anglers hide from players and use a bait creature, generally something that looks like a lower-level monster of the same zone. When they attack they reveal themselves and the lure dies. Prima table: scourgin 6, 7. ZAM cmob=4330 (Wayback 2003-09-14), comment by FirstAndOnly 2003-01-03: you will not find them, they find you. In the spawn area you see many botonid seedlings but not the scourgin under them. When a seedling comes close to you it dies and the scourgin pops out, with the message 'The lure dissapears and the Scourgin jumps out at <name>!'. Reply by Ynnad 2003-08-25: at level 7 he was jumped by orange and red cons and suggests levels 6-9 (Prima stays authoritative at 6-7). Freddyshouse 2002-10-30 (Mythic AI notes): higher-level monsters use lower-level monsters as lures and ambush mid-encounter. ZAM: no scourgin loot.
ALREADY IMPLEMENTED: scripts/mobs/BotonidSeedling.cs, class DOL.GS.Scripts.BotonidSeedling : GameNPC, with brain DOL.GS.Scripts.DOL.AI.Brain.BotonidBrain (AggroLevel 100, AggroRange 500, ThinkInterval 1000). Once the seedling has aggro and is within 150 of its target, it morphs into the scourgin (model 914) and announces it. After 30 s out of combat it morphs back into a seedling. Respawn 90 s. It is unused today: 0 of the 90 live seedlings have this ClassType.
FIXES NEEDED TO MATCH THE PERIOD: (1) AddToWorld calls LoadTemplate(60165666), so the lure gets the scourgin's level (6-9) and cons orange or red. The period lure looks like a lower-level monster. Keep the seedling's own row level (3) until the reveal, then set the level to 6-7 (Prima). (2) Bug: Transform() is called inside foreach (player in 400 radius), so with 2 or more players nearby it flips scourgin, seedling, scourgin... Send the message to each player, but call Transform once, outside the loop. (3) On reveal set Faction 100 (Predators of Hy Brasil) and Size to the template's 23-28 (the code uses 50). On revert set Faction 69 and Size 9. (4) Message: use the period wording 'The lure disappears and the scourgin jumps out at <name>!' (ZAM 2003), sent once to players within 400. (5) 'The lure dies': there is no XP and no seedling loot at the reveal. The killed scourgin gives its own XP and coin (no item loot per ZAM; template BodyType 0). (6) Keep the respawn at the row's 80-90 s and the 30 s out-of-combat revert. Optional, more faithful: spawn a separate scourgin NPC from template 60165666 at the lure's spot and make the lure vanish. No despawn or time-of-day behaviour is known.
monsters.notes: Placement means turning on the existing BotonidSeedling script on the lure seedlings by the two Prima SCOURGIN labels. monsters.script:
TWO PERIOD APPEARANCES.

(A) STATIC (Swett branch), already implemented. Live GameNPC row 8cfe3126 at 404113,400086,3256 (faction 20). Kill target of DataQuest 20045 step 6, which drops cq_apprentice_s_rod_of_necromancy. classic-quests.json quest 20045 step 6 Marker points at it. Period behaviour:
- a drakoran guardsman links with him. Warcry 957: 'As you attack the necromancer, a drakoran guard will come to help him'. Its NOTES add: 'If you solo pull the guardsman, the Apprentice Necromancer will not baf with him'.
- This already works through shared faction 20 with guardsman 99993662 at 404681,400864. No code is needed.

(B) QUEST-SUMMONED (Grym branch), NEEDS NEW DATA plus a small code check.
Period evidence:
- Allakhazam bestiary cmob 5001, updated 2003-07-01, Wayback capture 2003-10-11: 'Only spawns when you turn in the "bronze dark sword of Arawn" to Warin Grym for the Zombies, Ghosts, and Necromancers quest. If given a chance he will use a nasty DD ... took a lvl 50 armsman ~4 min to kill him soloing ... appears to have a lot of hitpoints'. It also says 'Con'd yellow to a lvl 50', with a level range of 46-50.
- Freddyshouse 2003-02-22: the group waited 40 minutes at the drakoran camp, 'but he spawns at the houses. So look there.'

monsters.script:
ENCOUNTER: Hamorik's emergence at the broken tower ritual area, Caldey (region 51, zone 54).

PERIOD EVIDENCE:
(a) SI Prima (2002), Caldey 'Enhanced Monster AI / The Right Place at the Right Time': if you find the ritual area you may witness his emergence; a spectacular lightshow starts, and if you are there when he arrives 'the real fun begins'.
(b) The SI Prima Caldey monster table lists four controller mobs: Hamorik Summoning L50, Invis Dead Check L50, Lich Effects (no level), Tower Spirit L0. Illia data (4 Jan 2003; Wayback captures 2003-07 to 2003-11-01) has the same names and types: Hamorik Summoning = Magical L50; Invis Dead Check = Undead L50; Lich Effects = Undead L1; Tower Spirit = Undead L0. All are Albion and none has loot or comments, so they are internal, unkillable helpers.
(c) Allakhazam Caldey zone comment, 17 Jul 2003: 'the broken tower in cadley ... the one with the light show at night'.
(d) Freddyshouse, Aug 2003: L61, nobody could find him (rare, short window).
No period source gives adds, health-% phases, special attacks, an exact duration or a respawn time. Do NOT invent adds.

IMPLEMENTATION (all new code; nothing exists yet):
1. Spawn row: ONE Mob row at the broken tower, 371520,411072,3486, heading 831, region 51, ClassType 'DOL.GS.HamorikRitual'. This new controller merges Tower Spirit, Lich Effects, Hamorik Summoning and Invis Dead Check into one class. Its brain is set in AddToWorld, e.g. 'DOL.AI.Brain.HamorikRitualBrain'; the Brain column can stay empty, the same pattern as VetustaAbbeyBell.cs. The controller is invisible and untargetable: Model 667 'Invisible Warrior' or 1, Flags CANTTARGET|DONTSHOWNAME|PEACE (60), name 'Tower Spirit', level 0. Base the brain on APlayerVicinityBrain (VetustaAbbeyBell.cs), so it only thinks with a player nearby; this keeps it light at bot scale.
2. Trigger: Region.IsNightTime turns true (WorldMgr day/night cycle; see Vortanos.cs / NightSpawnBrain in scripts/mobs/TimeDependentSpawnNpc.cs). Hamorik must not be alive, his respawn timer must have run out (Mob RespawnInterval 3600 s, or ServerProperties SET_EPIC_GAME_ENCOUNTER_RESPAWNINTERVAL like Vortanos/Colialt), and a player or bot must be within ~3000 of the tower. At most once per night.
3. Lightshow (Tower Spirit / Lich Effects / Hamorik Summoning): about 30-60 s of repeating spell-effect animations on the controller, sent to players within ~3000 via SendSpellEffectAnimation (pattern: MorganaBechardSilcharde.cs MorganaBrain, effect 9103 and ECSGameTimer sequencing). Optionally add a zone or area message. Period sources give neither the exact effect IDs nor the duration; choose lich-style effects from the real 1.64 spell table.
4. Emergence: when the show ends, spawn Hamorik at the tower centre. Use a new class 'DOL.GS.Hamorik : GameEpicBoss' (gameobjects/GameEpicBoss.cs) with brain 'DOL.AI.Brain.HamorikBrain : StandardMobBrain'. Level 61, BodyType Humanoid (6), model 61 (or 441), size 60, speed 250, AggroLevel 100, AggroRange ~600. LoadedFromScript = true and RespawnInterval -1: the controller owns the respawn. Stats come from the Vortanos family or a new NpcTemplate. Do NOT copy Vortanos's adds; there is no period evidence of any. He attacks whoever is present.
5. Invis Dead Check: the controller polls about every 5 s. If Hamorik is dead, start the respawn timer and wait for a later night. If Hamorik is alive, out of combat and day has come (IsNightTime false), remove him from the world (RemoveFromWorld, no loot) and re-arm for the next night. The night-only despawn is inferred from the 'at night' comment, not stated outright. Leash/reset: like Vortanos/Colialt, return to the tower and heal fully when aggro is lost.
6. Loot: none is attested in period. Dread Flail is attested only in 2004 (owner decision). Coin uses the normal L61 formula.

REUSABLE PIECES ALREADY IN THE SOURCE:
- GameEpicBoss
- Region.IsNightTime
- TimeDependentSpawnNpc / NightSpawnBrain (scripts/mobs/TimeDependentSpawnNpc.cs)
- Vortanos.cs (day/night toggling, add cleanup, reset on leash)
- Colialt.cs (an event-style SI epic in Albion SI; kills its adds in Die)
- MorganaBechardSilcharde.cs (ritual controller: effects, timers, restart)
- VetustaAbbeyBell.cs (invisible APlayerVicinityBrain controller row with flags 60 and game-hour checks)

1) Ranged fire: he casts a heat bolt using ClientEffect 313 (the existing 'Fireball' spell 313 is DamageType 13 Heat, Bolt, range 1875). Evidence: Prima p.136 'Hurling great balls of fire'; Zam 5817 'Throws balls of fire!' (Wayback 2003-09-14). No source gives damage, cast time or frequency. 2) Adds 'obsidian doomward': Prima p.136 says 'In times of need, obsidian doomward spawns run to his side in battle'. Trigger: while he is in combat ('in battle') and wounded ('in times of need'). Suggested gates: 75%, 50% and 25% health, one wave each. The percentages and the wave size (2 per wave) are NOT in any period source; they are a programmer/owner choice. Each doomward spawns at one of the anchors below (the outer ring of the caldera, 800-1400 units out), runs to him, then aggroes his current target (UlfketillBrain/LokenBrain pattern: AddToAggroList(target)). Spawn anchors are the live caldera lord positions, which have known Z: (361569,311561,3896), (360559,310262,3903), (362592,310212,3916).
3) BAF: the caldera lords around him are Social (Zam cmob=4613). Add any caldera lord within 1500 to his aggro on pull, ChiefTarekBrain style (bring-a-friend by brain/PackageID).
4) Reset/despawn: when the fight is over (reuse EpicEncounterMechanics.FightIsOver(boss), 8 s quiet), walk home, heal to full, and remove living doomwards. On his death the remaining doomwards keep fighting, then despawn when out of combat. Period sources do not say either way.
5) Respawn: no period source gives one; 1800 s follows the Prima batch convention for named. Group size from Prima: 'a full group of 45+ players, or two groups of lower 40s'. Freddyshouse 2003-03-11: 'lvl 65+ ... 1fg should be able to drop the big guy'.
